root.name: Neo-Grünfeld Defense: with Nf3
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nf3 d5

overview: Black meets 3.Nf3 with ...d5 in Grünfeld style. The most common continuation is the Neo-Grünfeld with 4.g3 Bg7 5.Bg2 O-O 6.O-O, where White fianchettoes and Black decides between ...dxc4, ...c6 or ...Nbd7. White can instead take on d5 and play e4 for a Grünfeld proper. No subtree data was supplied, so the branch is read from the moves.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto with g3 and Bg2, castle and keep a flexible centre
Pressure d5 and recapture on c4 for a queenside edge

black_ideas.idea: Fianchetto the bishop to g7 and challenge the centre with ...dxc4 or ...c5
Use ...Bg7 on the long diagonal against the d4 point

typical_structures.structure: Neo-Grünfeld: d4/c4 against d5/g6 with both bishops fianchettoed

character.notes: Strategic play with tension on c4/d5; less forcing than the Exchange Grünfeld.

soundness.notes: A mainstream line for both sides.

structure.notes: Centre tension on c4 and d5 is unresolved; a flexible centre.

level.notes: Positional manoeuvring with transpositions to know.

sublines_that_differ.name: Exchange Grünfeld transposition
sublines_that_differ.how: Gives a Grünfeld proper with White's big centre.
